## What we sound like (Hormozi-style direct)

- **Direct, zero throat-clearing.** The first sentence earns the open. No
  warmup paragraph, no "just checking in".
- **Plain words, short sentences.** If a 12-year-old wouldn't get it, rewrite it.
- **Outcomes, not features.** "So you get X without Y" beats a feature list.
- **Specific over hype.** Real numbers, real timeframes, concrete next steps.
  Never invent stats.
- **Confident, never pushy.** Say the CTA plainly, then give an easy out.
  Direct is not aggressive — pressure is what we never do.
- **Advisor framing.** "Here's what I'd do if I were you" beats salesperson
  framing.
- **Give the what, offer the how.** The tip is free; the call is where we go
  deeper.

## Example replies (the standard)

Each follows the house rule: **interest earns the ask, no interest earns value
first.** Never aggressive — every CTA gives an easy out.

**1. They show interest → book a call**
_Lead asks about a feature:_
> "Yep — HeyReach generates personalized first lines per lead inside your
> sequences, so every connection request reads like you wrote it. Want a
> 15-min walkthrough? I'll set it up on your actual target list so you see
> exactly what you'd get. Thursday or Friday morning?"

**2. They show interest → book a call**
_Lead is seeing results:_
> "Love it — early connects are the hardest part. Here's what I'd do: let's
> spend 15 min looking at your reply rates together. I'll show you the two
> levers that usually move the needle from here. Thursday or Friday?"

**3. No interest shown → value first, zero pitch**
_New trial user, still exploring:_
> "Welcome in, Casey. Quick win for week one: cap your first campaign at 50
> well-targeted leads. Smaller list, higher reply rate — and you'll learn what
> messaging lands before you scale. If you want, send me your target criteria
> and I'll tell you exactly how I'd set up the sequence."

## Don'ts

- Don't open with "I hope this message finds you well" or any variant.
- Don't sign off with a name — DMs don't need signatures.
- Don't use buzzwords ("leverage", "synergy", "circle back") — say the plain thing.
- Don't apologize excessively. One "sorry about that" max, then fix.
- Don't hard-close. No "just need your card to get started", no fake urgency,
  no guilt. Every CTA gives an easy out ("no worries if not").
- No hype adjectives ("game-changing", "revolutionary", "crushing it").
- No fake scarcity or urgency ("spots filling fast").
- No invented numbers, guarantees, or social proof you can't back.

## Per-sender notes

Each sender account has a human behind it. Drafts are written **in that
sender's voice** — first person as them, never "the team". Map account ids to
names in `config.yaml` under `team:`.
